behavioral_effects: New CI job compose runs make compose-check over every stack and profile combination on every push and PR; compose-check and compose-check-prod declare ci_job compose
test-frontend runs make frontend-format-check and make frontend-build after the unit tests; new validators frontend-format and frontend-build
security runs make audit-python (gating) and make audit-js (non-gating for now); new validator dependency-audit covers both
Exception preflights-are-host-only records why the five preflight validators keep ci_job null; validators-declare-their-ci-job now references it
.github/dependabot.yml proposes weekly grouped updates for uv (backend, governance tool), bun (frontend), npm (chrome-devtools sidecar), docker (four contexts) and github-actions
frontend README.md and e2e/chat.spec.ts reformatted by prettier; frontend/.governance.json is prettier-ignored because its shape belongs to the governance tool
compatibility_impact: codecov.yml is added to the read gate always_allow list (the Phase 0 CI run proved the fail-closed read-surface check works: it rejected the untracked-then-committed file). frontend/** is now text eol=lf in .gitattributes; existing Windows checkouts keep CRLF working copies until the tree is refreshed (git ls-files -z frontend | xargs -0 rm -f; git checkout -- frontend), which was done on this machine. compose-check-prod now includes the codecov profile in its description.
follow_up: Bump the frontend transitive dependencies bun audit flags (sharp, vitest, next-intl, js-yaml, esbuild, postcss, nanoid, opentelemetry) and the hono advisory in docker/mcp/chrome-devtools, then remove continue-on-error from the audit-js step
Rename docker/mcp/docling/requirements.lock to requirements.txt (or add a pyproject) so Dependabot's pip ecosystem can see it
Phase 2: governance-tool ruff and coverage floor with a Codecov governance flag, --since plumbing, the coverage-floor-does-not-regress check, new_file_gate tests
limitations: Simplification pass: not run; the diff is workflow, Makefile and governance-data plumbing plus two prettier reformat commits
Phase 1 of the CI/CD coverage plan. Not here: governance-tool lint and coverage, the coverage ratchet check, hygiene job, docker matrix and GHCR publish, e2e, nightly
reason: Eight registered validators declared ci_job null and only one had a recorded reason; compose-check and compose-check-prod need nothing but the docker CLI an ubuntu runner already has, next build and prettier were never run anywhere but the Dockerfile and Vercel, and pip-audit covered only the backend lockfile while tools/repo_governance/uv.lock, docker/mcp/docling/requirements.lock and docker/mcp/chrome-devtools/package-lock.json went unaudited. After this change the compose matrix, the production frontend build, the prettier check and every dependency set are exercised on every push and PR, the five preflight validators carry one reviewed exception explaining why they are host-only, and Dependabot proposes updates for each ecosystem.
risks: bun audit is non-gating until the frontend transitive findings are bumped; the follow-up must flip continue-on-error off within a week or the step becomes a badge nobody reads
Dependabot's bun ecosystem is newer than its npm one; if it rejects the frontend entry, switch that entry to Renovate or npm-on-package.json
docker/mcp/docling/requirements.lock is not a filename Dependabot pip discovers, so that set is audited by CI but not proposed for updates
rollback: git revert. Dependabot stops on the next scan once .github/dependabot.yml is gone; nothing else lives outside the repository.
security_impact: None new. Dependabot proposes and never merges. The audit surface widens from one lockfile to four; audit-js is visible but non-gating, which is stated in the workflow, the Makefile and the validator description so it cannot pass for a gate.
summary: Add compose validation, frontend build and format checks, and dependency audits over every lockfile to CI, and record why the preflight validators stay host-only
